what_it_is.prose: The Sukhoi Su-30MKI (NATO reporting name Flanker-H) is a twin-engine, multirole air superiority fighter operated by the Indian Air Force (IAF). The Su-30MKI is a variant of the Russian Su-30 specifically customized for India with thrust-vectoring engines, canards, and an international avionics suite (Russian, Indian, French, and Israeli components). India contracted the Su-30MKI in 1996 and HAL began license-building the aircraft at its Nasik division, with engine assembly at HAL Koraput (Orissa). Over 270 Su-30MKI have been delivered to the IAF, with a target of 318 aircraft making it the backbone of the IAF fighter fleet. The Su-30MKI is powered by two Saturn AL-31FP thrust-vectoring turbofan engines (Russia), license-assembled by HAL Koraput. The aircraft has a maximum speed of Mach 2.0 (2,120 km/h), range of 3,000 km with ferry tanks, and service ceiling of 17,300 m. Armament includes a 30mm GSh-30-1 cannon, R-77/R-27/R-73 air-to-air missiles, the BrahMos-A air-launched supersonic cruise missile (India-Russia JV), Kh-59ME and Kh-31P air-to-surface missiles, and KAB-500/1500 laser-guided bombs. The current indigenous content is approximately 50-60%; the 'Super Sukhoi' upgrade programme (under discussion) aims to increase this to 78% with indigenous AESA radar (Uttam), indigenous EW suite, and other Indian systems. The Su-30MKI was used in Operation Sindoor in May 2025, conducting air-launched BrahMos strikes. The aircraft is the IAF's primary air superiority fighter, complemented by the Rafale (Omnirole), MiG-29UPG, Mirage 2000I/H, and Tejas Mk-1A.

faq.question: What is the 'Super Sukhoi' upgrade?
faq.answer: The 'Super Sukhoi' is a planned upgrade programme for the IAF's Su-30MKI fleet aimed at extending the aircraft's service life and increasing indigenous content from the current ~50-60% to a target of 78%. Key upgrades include the indigenous Uttam AESA radar (replacing the Russian N011M Bars), an indigenous electronic warfare suite, new weapon integration (including Astra Mk-2/3 BVRAAMs), and modernised cockpit displays. The upgrade timeline has not yet been finalised as of August 2026.

faq.question: Was the Su-30MKI used in Operation Sindoor?
faq.answer: Yes. The Su-30MKI was used in Operation Sindoor in May 2025, conducting air-launched BrahMos-A supersonic cruise missile strikes. The Su-30MKI is the primary launch platform for the BrahMos-A — the air-launched variant of the BrahMos cruise missile. India signed a ₹2,500 crore contract in 2024 for the air-launched BrahMos upgrade programme.

faq.question: Where is the Su-30MKI license-built in India?
faq.answer: The Su-30MKI is license-built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) at two divisions: HAL Nasik (Maharashtra) handles final aircraft assembly, and HAL Koraput (Orissa) handles license assembly of the Saturn AL-31FP thrust-vectoring engines. HAL Nasik also performs overhauls and upgrades of the Su-30MKI fleet. License production began in 2000, with over 270 Su-30MKI delivered to the IAF as of 2026.
